transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ruth Bennett (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Aurora PM), Marcus Yu (Aurora Integration Eng), Priya Singh (Aurora Security), Tomás Alvarez (Aurora Marketplace Ops)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync to align on Redwood listing in AuroraCloud Marketplace, integration steps for reference architecture, packaging/container constraints, and security/KMS requirements. Action items capture deliverables and dates.

Topics: marketplace listing flow, reference architecture, container image sizes, KMS/encryption, deployment options (private vs managed), billing/integration, testing/QA and joint PR materials.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: hey everyone thanks for joining this is Jamie from Redwood, quick run though agenda, I think Samir will lead on the arch and then we'll triage marketplace reqs
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: thanks Jamie, yes we want to get a clean path for listing Redwood as an integrated inference offering inside Aurora marketplace — ideally public listing plus a reference-arch that shows on-prem and VPC flow
[00:25] Samir Patel: cool, I'll start with the reference arch, so the high level is we provide a containerized model runtime and a control-plane connector, for Aurora marketplace we typically ship a helm chart and a container image. we recommend a sidecar for metrics and a small init to do license validation
[00:41] Marcus Yu: sidecar ok, any constraints on image size? Aurora's registry has a 2GB soft limit for marketplace images, and our marketplace team prefers single-image artifacts but supports helm bundles
[00:55] Samir Patel: 2GB should be fine if we use quantized weights and layer squashing; our recommended base is the q8_0 profile which drops a lot of size. we can also split the weights into an OOB artifact fetched at install time if needed, we did that in another integration with CloudPeak
[01:15] Tomás Alvarez: fetching OOB assets is acceptable but we need a deterministic checksum and a secure download path, marketplace policy requires signed manifests and a digest pinned in the listing
[01:27] Ruth Bennett: noted, we'll produce a sha256 manifest and provide an S3 signed URL example in the reference-arch docs
[01:33] Priya Singh: quick security Q — how is customer data handled? we need to confirm encryption at rest, KMS integration and that no PII leaves the customer's VPC for private deployments
[01:47] Samir Patel: for Redwood Private the control plane is customer-managed and all inference traffic can stay in the VPC, by default we store minimal telemetry (metrics) and logs can be optional. encryption at rest is supported via KMS and HSM integrations, though we'll need to map to Aurora's KMS API for the marketplace flows
[02:03] Priya Singh: when you say KMS integration, are you using an in-house Redwood KMS connector or do you let customers supply their own key? we require customer-managed keys in our marketplace unless the partner is fully vetted
[02:17] Samir Patel: customers supply their own keys, Redwood supports both bringing-your-own-KMS and using a Redwood-managed key for hosted customers. for marketplace we will document the BYOK flow and sample KMS policy bindings (IAM + key policy)
[02:28] Lena Ortiz: good, also need to cover audit logs and SOC2 artifacts, marketplace listing requires attestation statements
[02:35] Jamie Park: we can provide SOC2 Type II summary, ISO certs and an SOC bridge doc, I'll attach the security pack; Samir will include the audit-log export options
[02:45] Marcus Yu: on deployment modes, we need the reference arch to show both - a managed integration (Aurora deploys on their infra) and a bring-your-own (customer on-prem/VPC with private control plane). the listing should clearly call out network requirements like outbound ports and NAT rules
[03:01] Samir Patel: absolutely, we'll include a network appendix: ports 443 outbound for control-plane comms, optional SSH for support, and mention KV cache persistence and session resumption behavior which could affect firewall configs
[03:17] Tomás Alvarez: do you have sizing guidance? CPU/GPU per throughput token rate? marketplace customers always ask for a T-shirt sizing model
[03:25] Ruth Bennett: yes we'll add a sizing table — e.g., for g4dn-like instances with a small batching profile, expect 20-30 qps for a 2k token average, for dedicated GPU pools we provide throughput curves. note that latency/cost tradeoffs will be documented
[03:45] Marcus Yu: packaging question — do you have a preferred Helm chart repo format? Aurora marketplace ingests OCI-based helm charts, but we also accept a custom bundle if partners need lifecycle hooks
[03:56] Samir Patel: we use standard Helm v3 charts published as OCI artifacts; we can also provide a Terraform module if Aurora wants to integrate provisioning into the marketplace console
[04:07] Priya Singh: another security item — secrets handling inside the chart. we require partners to use Aurora's secret manager integration rather than storing plain secrets in values.yaml. can Redwood support that pattern?
[04:20] Samir Patel: yes, we can template values to accept secretRef from Aurora's secret manager; we'll provide examples and a small init container that pulls keys at startup. for KMS, we'll document the IAM roles and KMS grants required
[04:33] Lena Ortiz: great. on billing, the marketplace wants a clear representation of pricing — do you support subscription + usage hybrid? customers sometimes want committed reserved pools plus pay-as-you-go burst
[04:47] Jamie Park: Redwood supports reserved capacity and hosted usage billing; marketplace listing can present both: a subscription package for reserved pools (Redwood Dedicated) and a hosted API option. we'll share sample SKUs and a pricing doc
[05:01] Tomás Alvarez: please include example invoices and a mapping of consumption metrics — we need tokens-per-invocation definition for billing reconciliation
[05:10] Ruth Bennett: we'll include a metrics export spec: tokens_consumed, request_count, avg_latency, model_version — exported via Prometheus and a JSON billing export for reconciliation
[05:22] Marcus Yu: on testing/QA, Aurora will run a compatibility test in our staging marketplace. what's the typical smoke test?
[05:30] Samir Patel: smoke tests include healthcheck endpoints, a standard generate request for a model with a short prompt, performance harness that validates p99 latency under synthetic load. we can provide a jenkins/golang runner or a simple k6 script
[05:44] Lena Ortiz: can you also provide a short demo video and a README we can show to internal reviewers? marketplace ops wants marketing assets too
[05:51] Jamie Park: yes, we have a 3-minute demo and a one-page reference-arch PDF; I'll upload links after the call.
[05:58] Tomás Alvarez: one nit — marketplace policy requires that partners declare third-party models or open-source licenses in the listing; do you have a license manifest?
[06:08] Ruth Bennett: we keep a BOM and license manifest, we'll include it. note some model weights are under custom licenses, we'll flag those accordingly
[06:15] Priya Singh: on the KMS question earlier, can Redwood support HSM-backed keys for key usage attestation? we need FIPS requirements for certain customers
[06:25] Samir Patel: yes, Redwood supports HSM-backed keys via integration with AWS CloudHSM and other providers; we'll document the config for FIPS mode and any perf implications — HSM can add latency to key unwrap ops so worth noting
[06:41] Marcus Yu: cool — also want to confirm rollback strategy for upgrades pushed via the marketplace: how do you handle model rollback and config migrations?
[06:51] Ruth Bennett: the helm chart supports canary upgrades and automatic rollback on failing health checks; for model weights we recommend weight versioning with a fallback alias that can be swapped atomically
[07:03] Jamie Park: ok we're at about 62 minutes, quick recap and next steps — Samir will share the reference architecture (diagram + helm snippets) by Friday 6/25, Ruth will include license manifest and metrics export spec, Jamie will send security pack and pricing template. Aurora will share marketplace onboarding checklist and image constraints by 6/28
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, appreciate the level of detail, this should make the listing review fast
[07:27] Tomás Alvarez: we'll schedule the staging compatibility window for first week of July, I'll send a calendar invite
[07:33] Jamie Park: perfect, thanks all, we'll follow up in writing and post docs to the shared link
